description: The bar chart titled “Average Entropy Across Sycophancy Reduction Methods on Static Experiments” visually compares the average entropy values of three sycophancy reduction methods — Baseline (pink), Source Info (beige), and Direct Command (light blue) — across three different AI models: GPT-4, Claude, and Llama, which are labeled along the horizontal axis. The vertical axis, labeled “Entropy Average Values,” ranges from 3.0 to 6.0 in increments of 0.5, representing the entropy metric used to quantify sycophancy. For each model, the three methods are grouped side-by-side, with the Baseline consistently showing the lowest entropy (around 4.8–4.9), Source Info the highest (around 5.1–5.2), and Direct Command intermediate (around 5.0–4.8). Notably, for GPT-4, Source Info reaches approximately 5.2, the highest value in the chart, while for Llama, Baseline drops to about 4.6, the lowest. The legend in the upper right corner clearly maps each color to its corresponding method, and the bars are uniformly spaced with no additional annotations or error bars. The chart suggests that Source Info tends to increase entropy (possibly indicating reduced sycophancy) relative to Baseline, while Direct Command shows mixed results depending on the model.
